findings.title: Production `BehavioralProfile` call site in `build_profiles()` is not covered — the server will raise `TypeError` at startup
findings.description: Task 2.2 scopes the update to *"all `BehavioralProfile` call sites **in tests**"* and lists only test files. `src/migratory_server/simulation.py:18-25` constructs `BehavioralProfile(max_speed=…, query_radius=…, cohesion_weight=…, separation_weight=…, alignment_weight=…, separation_radius=…)`. The slice design mandates the two new fields be **required with no defaults**, so this call raises `TypeError: missing 2 required positional arguments`. Consequences: `Server.run()` (`src/migratory_server/server.py:71`) fails at startup, `tests/test_simulation.py::TestBuildProfiles` (3 tests) fail, and `tests/test_main.py::test_starts_with_default_config` fails because the subprocess exits non-zero — i.e. Section 6.1 cannot pass. A task must update this call site and decide explicitly how the herding weights reach it: either extend `ProfileConfig` (`src/migratory_server/config.py:51`) + `config/default.yaml` with `leadership_weight`/`momentum_weight`, or pass `0.0` for both in `build_profiles()`. Note that `ProfileConfig` currently defaults the flocking weights to `0.0` in `_validate_profile()`, so there is precedent for either route — but the decision must be recorded, not left implicit. (The `ProfileConfig`/config-schema route also touches `config/default.yaml`, which no task mentions.)

findings.title: `EntityManager.spawn_population()` merges AgentState arrays manually and omits the new `leadership` array
findings.description: `spawn_population()` bypasses `add_agent()`/`remove_agent()` and concatenates `positions`, `velocities`, `accelerations` and `profile_indices` directly onto `self._state`. After Task 1.1 adds `leadership` to `AgentState`, this merge leaves `state.leadership` at its original length (0 on a fresh manager) while `state.count` becomes 100 — the SoA invariant ("all arrays length N") is broken. `LeadershipForce` then does `state.leadership[neighbors]` and will `IndexError` on any neighbor index ≥ the leadership array length. `EntityManager.spawn_population()` is called at server startup (`src/migratory_server/server.py:78`), so this is the live path, and it is exactly the path slice 107 (migration) and slice 103 (pack leaders) depend on for "per-agent leadership available in `AgentState`". Task 1.1 only enumerates `create()`, `add_agent()` and `remove_agent()`. Add a task to update `spawn_population()`'s merge (including `leadership`), with a test asserting `state.leadership.shape == (state.count,)` after a population spawn.

findings.title: The slice design's "no nested Python loops" technical requirement is dropped from both force implementation tasks
findings.description: The slice design's Technical Requirements state: *"Both forces are vectorized within each agent's neighborhood — no nested Python loops."* The Slice 101 breakdown carried this as an explicit bullet in each force implementation task (*"Use vectorized NumPy within each neighborhood — no `for neighbor in neighbors` inner loop"*, 101-tasks §2.1/§3.1/§4.1). Tasks 3.1 and 4.1 here specify the formulas but never state the vectorization constraint, and nothing verifies it. Given the architecture's hot-loop goal (`project-documents/user/architecture/100-arch.behavior-engine.md:33`), a junior implementer could write a per-neighbour Python loop in `LeadershipForce` and still pass every listed check. Restore the vectorization bullet in 3.1 and 4.1.

findings.title: `neighbor_lists` alignment with a subset of active agents is not specified, risking an index bug in both forces
findings.description: `tick()` builds `neighbor_lists` **only for active agents**, in `eval_indices` order, so entry `list_idx` corresponds to `eval_indices[list_idx]`, not to agent `list_idx`. The existing flocking forces handle this with `for list_idx, agent_idx in enumerate(eval_indices)` (`src/migratory/engine/flocking.py:37-43`). Tasks 3.1 and 4.1 say only *"When `active_indices` is `None`, iterate over all agents"*, which leaves the natural-but-wrong implementation `neighbor_lists[agent_idx]`. That is silently correct when `active_indices is None` and wrong for any subset — exactly the case the slice's "Forces respect `active_indices`" success criterion covers, and the case where the misalignment would not be caught by the `active_indices` isolation tests if `neighbor_lists` were built for the full population. State the `enumerate(eval_indices)` pattern explicitly in both force tasks, and add a test that passes a subset `active_indices` with a `neighbor_lists` list of matching (not full) length.

findings.title: Profile-differentiation assertion is disjunctive and can pass without demonstrating a measurable difference
findings.description: Task 5.3 asserts *"herding heading variance < flocking heading variance, **or** herding mean eastward component > flocking mean eastward component"*. A disjunction of two different metrics is satisfiable by accident and does not establish the slice design's requirement that the two profiles *"produce statistically different movement patterns"*. Task 5.2's assertion (*"mean heading has positive x-component"*) is likewise satisfiable by the random initial velocities alone (~50% of random seeds) and therefore does not demonstrate a *leadership-caused* bias. Tighten to a single pre-declared primary metric (e.g. mean east-component of the final heading strictly greater in the herding run **and** the flocking control's east-component below a stated threshold), fix the seed for both runs, and state the metric and threshold up front so the test is deterministic rather than flaky.

findings.title: Missing CHANGELOG and status-update tasks (project convention for delivered slices)
findings.description: Every other completed slice includes a documentation close-out: slice 301 task §3.2 ("Update `CHANGELOG.md` with tick loop additions under `[Unreleased]`"), 302 §4.4, 303 §4.4, each also updating frontmatter `status: complete` / `dateUpdated`. The 102 breakdown ends at "6.3 Final commit — `docs: complete slice 102`" with no CHANGELOG entry and no status/`dateUpdated` update for either the task file or `project-documents/user/slices/102-slice.herding-and-leadership.md` (still `status: not_started`). Add a final documentation task covering the CHANGELOG entry (new forces, new `AgentState`/`BehavioralProfile` fields, new tests) and the frontmatter status updates. The final commit message should also use `chore:` (as 301/302/303 do) rather than `docs:` for a slice close-out that includes code.

findings.title: "Existing 80 tests" baseline in the task file is stale
findings.description: The context summary and Section 6.1 both say "existing 80" tests. That count was accurate at Slice 101 completion, but the world-server slices (300/301/302/303) added roughly 130 more; the current tree contains on the order of 213 test functions across `tests/` (e.g. `tests/test_config.py` ~45, `tests/test_entities.py` ~24, `tests/test_server.py` ~22, `tests/test_server_tick.py` ~18, `tests/test_simulation.py` ~15, `tests/test_state.py` ~18, plus the engine suites). Reword to "all existing tests" so the implementer is not surprised by the suite size — and because the two FAIL findings above surface as failures in `tests/test_simulation.py` and `tests/test_main.py`, which are not part of the "80".

findings.title: No scale/load verification for two additional per-agent forces; repo has no CI
findings.description: The architecture goal *"Support tens of thousands of agents at full behavioral fidelity on a single CPU process"* is the parent's stated goal, and this slice adds two more Python-level per-agent passes to the hot loop (five forces are now summed per tick). There is no `tests/load/` directory and no CI configuration anywhere in the repository (no `.github/`), so nothing gates regressions. The slice design itself sets no numeric NFR and the parent slice plan does not restate one, so this is not a missing deliverable for 102 — but it is worth raising for slice 105 (spatial query optimization), which will need a regression baseline that includes the herding forces.
